hints: Compare the positions of R and T along one complete wavelength.
From a crest, the next upward equilibrium crossing is three-quarters of a cycle later.
Multiply that fraction of a cycle by 360°.
walkthrough: R is at a crest. Moving right to T passes an equilibrium crossing, a trough, then the next upward equilibrium crossing.
This separation is three-quarters of a wavelength.

hints: The wave travels right, while particles of a transverse wave move vertically.
At T the profile slopes upward to the right.
For a right-travelling profile, the particle moves opposite to the local slope at that instant.
walkthrough: T is an equilibrium-position point on a transverse wave travelling to the right.
The portion of profile arriving from the left has a downward displacement immediately after this instant, so T begins to move downward.
Draw a vertical arrow pointing downward at T.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a vertical downward arrow at T.

hints: The 0.62 cm separation is not a full wavelength; identify its fraction from the crest at R to the upward equilibrium crossing at T.
Convert the measured separation to metres before calculating frequency.
Find wavelength first, then use f = v/λ.
walkthrough: From crest R to upward equilibrium crossing T is three-quarters of a wavelength, so λ = 0.62 cm × (4/3) = 0.827 cm.
The frequency is 33 Hz to two significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses v = fλ, or equivalently v = λ/T with f = 1/T.
Determines λ = 0.62 × 10⁻² × (4/3) m, or an equivalent 8.3 × 10⁻³ m value.

hints: At P, identify whether a crest from one source meets a crest or a trough from the other source.
Express this in terms of phase or path difference, then apply superposition to the two equal amplitudes.
State the amplitude at P, not just the type of interference.
walkthrough: At P a solid crest line from one source meets a dashed trough line from the other, so the waves arrive in antiphase.
Their path difference is an odd number of half-wavelengths; here it is 1.5 wavelengths.
By superposition, the resultant displacement is the sum of the two displacements. Equal and opposite displacements cancel.
The waves destructively interfere, so the resultant amplitude at P is zero at all times.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the resultant displacement is the sum of the two source displacements, or that the waves superpose at P.
Explains destructive interference at P through antiphase waves, a crest meeting a trough, or an odd-half-wavelength path difference.
States that the resultant amplitude is zero at all times.
